correctness.rationale: The theorem concerns all integers n>=7 for the bidirected K_{2,n} multipath complex, where every vertex has selected indegree/outdegree <=1 and selected directed cycles are forbidden. Verified the four-row by n chessboard A_n consists of faces with pairwise distinct arc rows and leaf columns. A nonchessboard face has a single admissible repeated-column directed two-path P_i Q_i or R_i S_i, and two bends cannot coexist. Each bend star is the cone e_i*L_i over the crown graph on 2(n−1) vertices and (n−1)(n−2) edges, and its intersection with A_n is ∂e_i*L_i≃ΣL_i. Other star overlaps lie inside A_n. For n≥7, Ziegler vertex-decomposability gives A_n a 3-sphere wedge and π_2(A_n)=0, so all suspended crown-graph attaching maps are null. The 2n cones contribute 2n(n²−5n+5) 3-spheres, and the chessboard Euler computation gives r(n)=n⁴−10n³+29n²−24n+1, hence R(n)=n⁴−8n³+19n²−14n+1. Independently enumerated complete face sets and F₂ boundaries for n=4..9 and reconstructed bend/link partition for n=4,7,8; stable ranks n=7/8/9 are 491/1105/2143. The infinite homotopy result relies on the checked structural argument and published theorem, not the finite computations.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality: this is a uniform non-equivariant homotopy classification for the bidirected complete bipartite K_{2,n}, n>=7. The primary full-text sources separately cover one-way complete bipartite orientations, bidirectional paths/polygons and the four-row chessboard core. The published bidirected double-star homotopy classification is on a different underlying tree; its theorems do not imply the symmetric biclique cone-attachment formula. Actual Resultary, published-result and primary literature comparisons supplied no mathematically dominating prior statement; absence in bounded search is not proof of global priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed theses, unpublished computations, recently revised work, and alternate names for multipath or chessboard complexes could contain an implication-equivalent theorem.
A higher-level general theorem for bidirected graph multipath complexes not identified by bounded searches might imply the n>=7 specialization.
Related low-width n<=6 biclique studies are not a proof for the infinite quantified range; their mathematical overlap remains acknowledged.
Originality is best-of-knowledge only, not an exhaustive priority or independent certification claim.

value.rationale: The family bidirected K_{2,n} is an unbounded natural class whose multipath complexes are not ordinary chessboard complexes because of two-arc same-leaf paths and directed two-cycles. This all-n>=7 integral homotopy classification reveals a stable torsion-free pure three-dimensional sphere-wedge regime and quantifies the extra 2n crown-graph contributions beyond the known chessboard core. The cutoff n=7 is mathematically dictated by shellability of the four-row core, not arbitrary numerical slicing. A researcher studying bidirectional digraph complexes or stability of graph-complex homotopy types could use this exact family result; it is not a standard renaming or small table recomputation.
residual_risks: No extension to n<7, higher hub number, equivariant splitting or arbitrary orientations is established; these are expressly outside the claim.

scientific_limitations: Non-equivariant geometric homotopy claim only; two hubs, all spokes bidirected, and n>=7.
Bounded enumerations establish n<=9 only; infinite conclusion rests on structural homotopy proof.
